search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting West Nile virus cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and surveillance data for California during August 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, subnational and local locations, and date reported.
search_reasoning: West Nile virus in California is primarily reported through CDPH (California Department of Public Health) and county-level health departments, with CDC ArboNET as the national surveillance backbone. August is peak WNV transmission season in California, so weekly or monthly surveillance bulletins from CDPH and county agencies are the highest-yield sources. The upstream planned queries use overly rigid quoted phrase constructions (e.g., "WNV California August 2024") that may suppress relevant results from official agency pages that use natural prose. This iteration replaces those with cleaner, more flexible queries targeting: (1) CDPH's WNV surveillance page and weekly reports, (2) CDC ArboNET/MMWR data for California 2024, (3) county-level health department reports (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern — historically high-burden counties), and (4) news/media reports citing official case counts for August 2024. The 4-query cap per iteration forces prioritization: official state agency first, CDC national surveillance second, high-burden county agencies third, and news/media fourth. Peer-reviewed literature is deprioritized for iteration 1 because August 2024 data would not yet be published in journals by any reasonable lag. Structured database queries are deferred to iteration 2 if official sources are insufficient.

query_batch.query: California West Nile virus cases deaths 2024 CDPH surveillance weekly report August
query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH publishes weekly WNV surveillance summaries during transmission season (typically May–October). This query targets the California Department of Public Health's official WNV reporting pages, which are the primary authoritative source for statewide case counts, deaths, and county-level breakdowns. 'August' and '2024' are included as unquoted terms to avoid over-constraining the query against pages that may use date ranges or cumulative language.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH West Nile virus surveillance bulletin or weekly update page listing case counts by county and week/month for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain, official surveillance report language, tabular case data with county breakdowns

query_batch.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus California 2024 cases neuroinvasive fever deaths statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV case counts including neuroinvasive disease, fever cases, and deaths. CDC's WNV statistics page is updated periodically and provides confirmed/probable breakdowns by state. This serves as a cross-validation source against CDPH data and may include August 2024 cumulative or monthly figures.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV statistics page or ArboNET data table showing California 2024 case counts by disease category (neuroinvasive, fever) and deaths
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, ArboNET attribution, tabular state-level data

query_batch.query: West Nile virus August 2024 California county cases deaths "Los Angeles" OR "Sacramento" OR "Kern" OR "Fresno" health department
query_batch.query_rationale: California WNV burden is concentrated in the Central Valley and Southern California. Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, and Fresno counties historically report the highest WNV case counts. County health departments often publish their own press releases or surveillance updates with locality-level data not disaggregated in state reports. This query targets those sub-state sources to populate the 'locality' field.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: County public health department press release, advisory, or surveillance update reporting WNV cases or deaths in August 2024 with specific locality or zip code data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: lacounty.gov, saccounty.gov, kernpublichealth.com, or similar county health domain; official press release format

query_batch.query_rationale: News articles published in August 2024 citing official health agency data can surface case counts, deaths, and locality details that link back to primary official sources. query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Publication date in August 2024; quotes attributed to CDPH, county health officer, or official spokesperson; numeric case/death figures

No Spanish-language or other localized query variants are needed for official surveillance data, though Spanish-language news sources (e.g., La Opinión) could be considered in iteration 2 if English-language news coverage is sparse.

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong signals from westnile.ca.gov (9 results including multiple weekly update PDFs with 2024 human case counts) and cdc.gov (4 results including ArboNET historic data), plus publichealth.lacounty.gov. However, the snippets show cumulative year-to-date figures (e.g., "112 human cases," "98 human cases") without confirmed August-specific breakdowns, weekly report dates, deaths, hospitalizations, or county-level disaggregation for the August 2024 window. Key gaps remain: (1) the specific westnile.ca.gov weekly update PDFs covering the August 1–31, 2024 window have not been identified by date — the download IDs (4980, 5061, 5072) need date anchoring; (2) deaths and hospitalizations for August 2024 specifically are not yet confirmed in snippets; (3) county-level data for Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, and other high-burden counties beyond LA is absent; (4) the CDC 2024 provisional data page (distinct from historic data) has not surfaced. Iteration 2 should: (a) target the westnile.ca.gov weekly archive index to identify August 2024 report dates, (b) target the CDC 2024 provisional WNV data page, (c) target Sacramento and Kern county health departments directly, and (d) target CDPH press releases confirming deaths in August 2024.
